title: Alphashot XL G2: product photos, dimensions, weight and data in a single cycle
h1: Alphashot XL G2: product photos, dimensions, weight and data in a single cycle
metaTitle: Alphashot XL G2: photos, dimensions, weight and data in one cycle
description: Studio photos, 360° spins, laser dimensions, weight and label reading in one cycle, up to 250 products a day: what the Alphashot XL G2 changes, and for whom.
author: Sébastien Jourdan
content:
The Alphashot XL G2 is an automated photo studio that captures, in a single cycle, both a product's images and its data: packshots, 360° spins, video, dimensions, weight, label data. You set the product down. You hit start. Everything comes out structured, ready to publish.

A system that photographs, measures and reads packaging in one handling — we'd been asked for it for years. Orbitvu built it.

The essentials in 20 seconds

  • One cycle: packshots, 360° spins, video, laser dimensions, weight, OCR label reading
  • Handles products up to 60 × 40 × 70 cm and 25 kg. Rule of thumb: if it fits in a cabin suitcase, it fits
  • Up to 250+ products a day with a single operator, no photography skills required
  • Relevant if you're in: logistics, distribution, food, healthcare, marketplace selling, resale, spare parts… and more
  • Built by Orbitvu, distributed, installed and supported in France and Switzerland by PackshotCreator

Why capture photos and data at the same time?

Right now you track your products every step of the way to going live:

  1. Photo studio for the visuals.
  2. More or less manual weighing and measuring of the product.
  3. And finally, someone re-keys the packaging into the system, line by line.

Three stations. Three handlings. At every handover, a chance to get it wrong, and time lost. One wrong dimension and it's the wrong box, the carrier dispute, the product return… and hours spent fixing the error and its fallout.

Automated photo studios industrialised the 'photo' station twenty years ago. The other two mostly stayed manual.

Today the Alphashot XL G2 handles all three of these strategic stations, in the time usually reserved for photography alone. Fewer errors, less logistical drag — the XL G2 belongs to that class of innovation whose need you never measured until it arrived, and which you can no longer do without once it's part of your day.

What exactly does the system capture?

Two variants, one platform. The Alphashot XL G2 handles the content: photos, 360°, video, label reading. The MDC version adds measurement. Two lasers read the dimensions, a scale housed under the turntable weighs the product. While the camera works, so do the lasers.

CaptureDetailWhat it changes
Photos, 360°, video170 AI-driven LED panels, motorised turntable accurate to 0.5°The 300th shot identical to the first, no photographer
Dimensions2 lasers, L × W × H, objects from 5 mm to 70 cmReliable freight pricing and warehouse slotting
WeightBuilt-in scale, accurate to 5 g, up to 25 kgNo more estimated weights that end in disputes
Label dataAI OCR: ingredients, barcodes, compliance statementsA compliant product sheet with no manual re-keying
ExportTo PIM, ERP, DAM: API, connectors, CSVData lands in your systems, not in a spreadsheet

One detail that isn't one: nothing is generated. The OCR reads what's printed on the packaging, and stops there. No invented text, no generative guesswork. The day someone asks where your allergen list comes from, the answer fits in a single sentence: from the packaging itself.

Who is the Alphashot XL G2 for?

Three situations. If you recognise yourself in one of them, this system was drawn for you.

Logistics, distribution, spare parts: dimensions that protect the margin

Do you pay or bill freight by volumetric weight? Then you already know. One centimetre of error across three axes, multiplied by thousands of parcels, ends up as a red line on the P&L. Plenty of warehouses have fitted cubing stations to firm up that data. Fine for measuring. Except none of them produces a sellable image, so you need a second pass — at the studio this time.

The XL G2 MDC does both at once. Dimensions and weight for the warehouse system, packshots and 360° for the e-commerce listing.

Who's concerned? Logistics and fulfilment providers, distributors feeding the GS1 data models, spare-parts catalogues, DIY superstores. Everyone, in short, for whom a dimension isn't a piece of information but a cost.

Food, healthcare, cosmetics, marketplaces: compliance without re-keying

The INCO regulation first: everything printed on a food package must appear on the product page, before purchase. The GPSR next, in force since December 2024: identification of the responsible person, warnings, traceability, for just about anything sold in Europe. Marketplaces don't argue. Incomplete listing, blocked listing.

So thousands of e-tailers re-key their packaging. By hand. An allergen list with a typo isn't a typo — it's a legal risk.

The XL G2's OCR settles the question at capture time: the statements come out structured, at the same moment as the photos. Food and click-and-collect, marketplace sellers, pharmacy, cosmetics and their INCI lists: this one is for you.

Resale, auctions, inventory: the one-off item finally worth it

Photographing a thousand all-different products is hard: in resale, each piece has to be photographed, measured, weighed, documented. One by one. You handle visuals case by case, bespoke. Orbitvu systems already knew how to optimise that, but integrating the dimensions, weight and timestamps alongside the visuals stayed manual.

And the market is pushing hard: 121 billion euros in Europe, 14% of e-commerce expected in 2026, according to Cross-Border Commerce Europe.

One cycle per item, and the piece comes out with its photos, its measurements, its weight. Timestamped. For resale and refurbished players, it's individual handling that becomes economically viable. For auction houses, experts and insurers, something else counts: an inventory record that holds up, in the spirit of evidential documentation.

What limits should you weigh before deciding?

Three checks, before going any further:

  • The size. 60 × 40 × 70 cm, 25 kg maximum. Beyond that, you need a large-format studio like the Alphastudio XXL.
  • The volume. Worth it? Yes, but not below a thousand products a year, per Orbitvu. Under that threshold, a classic studio and a tape measure still hold their own.
  • Your existing data. If dimensions and weight already arrive firmed up from your suppliers, the base variant, without the measurement module, will probably do.

A brand-new system, so no customer track record: how do you check?

True — but the gains are easy to measure: add up what the full journey of one of your products costs today. Handlings, measuring, re-keying, error corrections. Our return-on-investment calculator gives you the framework; the result often surprises.

And to see it with your own eyes: come for a demo with your products, and leave with your files. Images, measurements, data extracted from your real packaging. Thirty minutes, and you'll know whether the Alphashot XL G2 is right for you.

The last word

Twenty years ago, we were asked for beautiful photos, faster. The need has taken shape; today our customers ask for more: products ready to sell.

The Alphashot XL G2 is the first system to take that demand literally. For anything that fits in a cabin suitcase, a single handling is now enough — images and data included.

Sébastien Jourdan is the director of PackshotCreator – Sysnext, founder of blendai.studio and a photographer specialising in packshot photography for over 20 years.

faqs.question: Does the Alphashot XL G2 replace a cubing station?
faqs.answer: Yes, for products up to 60 × 40 × 70 cm and 25 kg — and it does more. A cubing station measures dimensions and weight for the warehouse, full stop. The XL G2 MDC captures those same data points and also produces, in the same cycle, packshots, 360° spins and videos ready to publish. For a logistics provider, measurement then changes status: from a cost centre, it becomes a billable service, since the same pass produces the clients' e-commerce content. Dedicated cubing systems keep their place for oversized parcels or in-conveyor measurement.

faqs.question: What's the difference between the Alphashot XL G2 and the MDC version?
faqs.answer: Both produce photos, 360° rotations and videos in an automated cycle, and read labels by OCR. The MDC version adds the measurement layer: two lasers for dimensions, a built-in scale for weight, captured at the same time as the images. The base model suits you if your reference data comes from elsewhere; MDC if you want to capture everything from the physical product, in one pass.

faqs.question: Can the extracted data feed a PIM or ERP directly?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Orbitvu Station software structures the measurements and label data, then exports them to your product repository (PIM), your management system (ERP) or your media library (DAM), via API, publishing connectors or CSV import. That's the whole point: no more re-keying between capture and your systems.

faqs.question: Can you bring a food product page into INCO compliance with this system?
faqs.answer: It's one of its most direct uses. The INCO regulation requires the packaging's mandatory statements (ingredients, allergens, nutritional values, quantities) to appear on the product page before the online purchase. The Alphashot XL G2's OCR reads those statements on the physical packaging during the shoot and returns them as structured data, with no re-keying. Nothing is generated or filled in: what's extracted is what's printed.

faqs.question: And what about the GPSR on marketplaces?
faqs.answer: The GPSR, in force since December 2024, requires you to display the responsible person's identification, warnings and traceability data; marketplaces block incomplete listings. Those statements are on the packaging, and that's exactly what the OCR captures and structures. The system doesn't replace your compliance analysis; it removes the re-keying step that makes it slow and error-prone.

faqs.question: Is it suited to resale and refurbished goods?
faqs.answer: It's even one of the most obvious use cases. Since each second-hand item is unique, photos, measurements and weighing have to be redone piece by piece; the single automated cycle makes that individual handling profitable. The item comes out photographed, measured, weighed and timestamped — which, along the way, documents its condition at the moment it went on sale.

faqs.question: Can the system's AI distort the product?
faqs.answer: No, and that's a design choice. The AI steps in during capture (lighting adjustment, cut-out, label reading), never afterwards to generate content. The real product stays the source of truth. For regulatory data, that counts double.
